name: Christmas
intro: The big day, the weekday, and the days left to get ready. Count down to Christmas morning wherever you are.
explanation_title: Same date. A different day of the week.
explanation: This countdown follows Christmas Day on December 25 in the Gregorian calendar. The date stays the same each year, while the weekday changes. Christmas Eve is December 24.
scope_note: Some Christian communities celebrate Christmas on a different date. This page tracks the December 25 observance, rather than an employer’s observed day off.
planning: Make separate countdowns for your last shopping day, your journey home, and Christmas dinner. Each can have its own reminder in the app.
source_label: US Office of Personnel Management: holiday dates

name: Halloween
intro: Costumes to plan. Pumpkins to pick. See which day Halloween falls on and how long you have to get ready.
explanation: Halloween’s calendar date stays the same each year, but its weekday changes. Use the upcoming dates to see whether the next Halloween falls during the week or on a weekend.
scope_note: Local trick-or-treat hours, school celebrations, and Halloween parties may use different dates or times. Check the organizer’s schedule for your plans.
planning: Count down to October 31, then add your own costume deadline or party date. Keep the one you’re most excited about on your Home Screen.

name: New Year
intro: Look ahead to January 1. See the next New Year’s date and count the days to a brand-new chapter.
explanation_title: A new year starts on January 1.
explanation: This page follows the Gregorian calendar. New Year’s Eve is December 31, and New Year’s Day begins at midnight immediately afterward. That moment arrives at different times around the world.
scope_note: The countdown uses your device’s local calendar date. It does not follow the midnight celebration in a particular city or the dates of Lunar New Year and other calendars.
planning: Add your New Year’s Eve party as its own event with a start time. Use another countdown for a January trip, a personal goal, or the first day of something new.
source_label: US Office of Personnel Management: holiday dates

name: Thanksgiving
answer_prefix: In the United States, Thanksgiving is on
intro: Start with the date. Make room for the plans. Count the days until Thanksgiving in the United States.
explanation: US Thanksgiving falls on the fourth Thursday in November. Because November begins on a different weekday from year to year, Thanksgiving’s date ranges from November 22 to November 28. It is not always the last Thursday of the month.
scope_note: This page is for US Thanksgiving. Canadian Thanksgiving follows a different calendar rule and is not the date shown here.
planning: Give your travel day, grocery shopping, and family meal their own countdowns. A reminder before each date can help spread the preparation across the week.
source_label: US Office of Personnel Management: Thanksgiving dates

name: Easter
rule_label: A Sunday between March 22 and April 25
intro: Find the next Easter Sunday, see future dates, and count the days until your spring celebration.
explanation_title: Why is Easter on a different date each year?
explanation: Western Easter uses a church calendar calculation involving an ecclesiastical full moon and a fixed March 21 equinox. It falls on a Sunday between March 22 and April 25. The calculation uses calendar rules rather than the exact full moon visible from your location.
scope_note: This page shows Western Christian Easter in the Gregorian calendar. Orthodox Easter may fall on a different Sunday. School breaks and public holidays also vary by location.
planning: Keep Easter Sunday separate from your school break, travel dates, and family gathering. Add the dates your school or organizer confirms to the app.
source_label: Royal Observatory Greenwich: how Easter is dated

name: Valentine’s Day
intro: A small surprise or a big night out. Find the date and count the days until Valentine’s Day.
explanation_title: February 14, whichever weekday it falls on.
explanation: Valentine’s Day is celebrated on February 14 each year. The weekday changes, so the table below can help you plan a meal, a trip, or time together.
scope_note: This page follows the February 14 celebration. If you celebrate on a nearby weekend or another date, create a separate countdown for those plans.
planning: Add a reminder for your reservation or gift, then keep your celebration date on a widget. You can also count up from the day your own story began.
source_label: Library of Congress: Valentine’s Day traditions

name: Mother’s Day
answer_prefix: In the United States, Mother’s Day is on
intro: See when Mother’s Day falls in the United States and how many days are left to make your plans.
explanation: In the United States, Mother’s Day falls on the second Sunday of May. Its date can range from May 8 to May 14, so it moves on the calendar while staying on a Sunday.
scope_note: Mother’s Day dates vary by country. This is the US date; it should not be used for the UK’s Mothering Sunday or assumed to apply everywhere.
planning: Plan a visit, a call, or time together. Add a separate reminder for sending a card or arranging flowers so the preparation has its own place on your calendar.
source_label: US Department of State: Mother’s Day and Father’s Day (PDF)

name: Father’s Day
answer_prefix: In the United States, Father’s Day is on
kicker: Make time for a good day together
intro: Find the US Father’s Day date and count the days until a visit, a meal, or a simple moment together.
explanation: In the United States, Father’s Day falls on the third Sunday of June. Its date ranges from June 15 to June 21, while the day of the week remains Sunday.
scope_note: Father’s Day is observed on other dates in some countries. This page tracks the US observance, so check the local date if you are planning a celebration elsewhere.
planning: Add your celebration and any preparation dates separately. A countdown to a visit or a shared activity can be a nice reminder of what’s coming up.
source_label: US Department of State: Mother’s Day and Father’s Day (PDF)
